title: The Sherpa Request That Became Hillary's First School at Khumjung
conflicts: Who asked for the school: Sirdar Urkien (Hillary's book, via Wikipedia), Konchok Chumbi (his son Ang Tshering Sherpa), an unnamed Sherpa friend (Himalayan Trust Nepal), a boy with a 60-name petition (NZ Herald), plus the elders' yeti-scalp condition (CSM, Wikipedia); the story sets out the differing accounts rather than choosing. Trust founding: 1963 registration (Himalayan Trust Nepal) vs 1964 (BBC); the Trust's 1963 given with attribution. First intake 40 (Hillary) vs 50 (unsourced snippet); 40 used. School totals 26/27/nearly 30; the Trust's 27 used.
notes: Hillary's own words come from a 2011 HuffPost piece quoting the author's earlier interview with him; his book Schoolhouse in the Clouds is not online, so Urkien rests on Wikipedia's citation of it (Wikipedia used once, supplementary). Te Ara, NZHistory and Papers Past block automated requests. Quote stance: affirms.
